# Vendor Room / Pricing Room

- Pricing Room presentation scopes its semantic palette to `.pricing-room`; planning estimates reuse the worksheet and shared margin utilities, never approval or checkout writes. Why: keep the redesign isolated and projections separate from verified financial decisions.
- Pricing Room uses its own bounded scrolling area with a sticky opaque summary, leaving the surrounding product layout unchanged. Why: keep price, projected results and protections visible without covering detail controls or changing the page shell.
- The Pricing Room wrapper (profit-breakdown-with-quotes.tsx) owns the destination choice and keys every query and the panel by destination; readiness and approval display only the server's evaluatePricingDestination result for the saved revision. Why: unsaved browser edits or another country's worksheet can never look approved.
- Editable costs, commission applicability, quoted method preference and private notes live in the existing product/destination inputs JSON and revision lifecycle; server saves reject new verified-cost declarations and derive summaries from source-backed calculations. Why: avoid parallel settings storage, forged verification and approval state surviving edits.
- The Vendor Room station keeps pilot and queue logic separate but shares ProductWorkspaceLayout for the pilot and Empress acceptance product; other queue behavior stays unchanged. Vendor options come only from persisted records. Why: staged presentation preserves functions without implying integrations or advancing all-product integration.
- Room-scoped vendor-workspace.css owns the white/gold presentation and native-size gallery; product owners retain all save, pricing, approval and handoff logic. Why: visual consolidation must not become a financial or permissions refactor.
